newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - soft, wondering about supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - soft, wondering about supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds shed around three basis points in muted trade on Friday, tracking similar results achieved by Treasuries and weighing the prospect issuers will seize on a big, recent drop in rates.
"Obviously, whenever rates drop this precipitously, a lot of refundings that had been on the margin sort of suddenly come into the money," said a senior municipal analyst at a brokerage house.

Since Monday, yields on the 30-year, bellwether Treasury bonds have fallen to 6.46 percent from 6.54 percent, in part due to the market's belief that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan has no near-term plans to tighten monetary policy.
While Treasury bond prices slipped on Friday, traders felt the market's recent bullish trend remained intact.

The Metropolitan Transportation Authority of the State of New York, seeking to take advantage of the strength in fixed-income markets, advanced to August 12 an approximately $400 million sale of new money bonds that had been slated for late August or early September.
The negotiated offering through Smith Barney also might include from $50 million to $100 million of refunding bonds.

Municipal bond sales for next week were expected to total $3 billion in 103 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. This was just over $1 billion more than seen on Thursday, in a preliminary forecast of supply.
Negotiated offerings total $2.033 billion in 51 sales, with a $340 million California Natural Resources offering through PaineWebber Inc., topping the list.
On the competitive side, 52 sales totaling $966 million are scheduled. A 250 million Maryland offering on Wednesday is the largest.

Secondary market activity was not particularly active ahead of the summer weekend, though the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List stood at nearly $1.4 billion. That was roughly $500 million above levels seen early last week.
Actively quoted issues included Atlanta, Georgia, Water and Sewer Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.37 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 5.45 percent, NET, up one basis point.

After an initial dip, the market discounted a surprising 2.3 percent rise in durable goods orders, like cars and refrigerators, in June, noting transportation orders, which make up about a fifth of the report, climbed 7.5 percent. Subtracting that component produced a rise of 0.08 percent, which economists said was consistent with moderate growth.
For the overall report, economists surveyed by Reuters had predicted only a 1.4 percent increase.

A decline in existing home sales during July largely was predicted by experts. The report showed they fell 2.6 percent to an annualized rate of 4.14 million. Economists had forecast the measure would slip to 4.19 million.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal futures closed off 10 ticks at 120-22/32, while September Treasury bonds fell nine ticks to 115-1/32. This left the MOB down a bit from levels seen early this week at plus 181 ticks.
